episodes.179322: A thunderstorm produced a strong wind gust off of the Brevard County coast.
episodes.179455: Sufficient lift ahead of an upper low over California and Arizona and Gulf moisture ahead of the dryline across eastern New Mexico allowed widespread showers and storms to initiate around midday. Several supercells produced large and severe hail along with two tornadoes in the central and south-central highlands of Guadalupe and Lincoln County. Later that evening, training supercells grew upscale into a convective complex with flash flooding across east central New Mexico.
episodes.179456: The upper level low from May 31st slowly moved northeast towards Colorado with another round of severe storms across eastern New Mexico. Training supercells in central and southern Guadalupe County resulted in several reports of 1 to 2 inch hail as well as heavy rain. There were no reports of flash flooding however.
episodes.179479: Landspout.  Trained weather spotter looking west from Walworth at the intersection of US Highway 14 and WI-67 reported a brief landspout with dust visible at the surface under a funnel.  No damage reported.  Report relayed via NWS Chicago.  Time and location estimated via radar.
episodes.179494: Rich moisture, a weak upper level disturbance, and several low-level boundaries worked in concert to bring torrential rainfall to portions of the south-central and southeastern South Plains on the first. One of the primary factors, in addition to the plentiful moisture, was a low-level boundary, originating from thunderstorm activity that affected the Texas Panhandle the previous evening into the overnight hours, that provided a focus for shower and thunderstorm development. Widespread and intense thunderstorms became anchored over the south-central South Plains including a good portion of Lynn County. Torrential rainfall rates continued for nearly two hours, from around 0830 CST to 1030 CST, before finally diminishing, then ending completely by early afternoon. The Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near O'Donnell measured 7.02 inches, much of which fell in the two hour window from mid to late morning. The area of heaviest thunderstorms eventually shifted northeastward late morning and early afternoon, dropping widespread three to four inch totals from Tahoka (Lynn County) to Post (Garza County). The intense rainfall rates and impressive rain totals led to significant flash flooding that affected much of US Highway 87 between Tahoka and Lamesa as well as US Highway 380 from Tahoka to east of Post. The rapid onset of flooding resulted in numerous vehicles becoming inundated by water on the highways and ultimately resulted in the closure of portions of US Highways 87 and 380 from the first into the second. Many water rescues occurred and many vehicles were stranded.
episodes.179538: The Merced River at Pohono Bridge peaked above it's flood stage of 10 feet each day between June 1 through June 7, June 10 through June 12 and June 14 through June 18. The Merced River at Happy Isles peaked near or above it's flood stage of 8 feet each day between June 14 through June 18.
episodes.179544: Isolated thunderstorms moved across parts of northeast Illinois during the afternoon of June 1st producing isolated hail and isolated wind damage.
episodes.179545: Isolated thunderstorms moved across parts of northwest Indiana during the afternoon of June 1st producing isolated hail and isolated wind damage.
episodes.179608: A thunderstorm became briefly severe over central Butte County, producing wind gusts around 60 mph.
episodes.179610: A thunderstorm became marginally severe over central Harding County, producing wind gusts near 60 mph.
episodes.179655: A pulse thunderstorm developed near Cecil (Shawano County) just south of Shawano Lake during the afternoon on Thursday (6/1).  The storm produced a downburst, which caused wind damage on Shawano Lake.
episodes.179996: Flooding on the James River which started in mid-April continued through the entirety of June, due to the combination of April snowmelt and rounds of heavy showers and thunderstorms during the middle to end of the month. Agricultural land and some county roadways continued to be significantly impacted.
episodes.179998: Scattered thunderstorms developed during peak heating of the afternoon in temperatures around or above 90 degrees, and intensified as they drifted west-northwest under the influence of a westward-moving high pressure center aloft. Strong to occasionally severe downdraft wind gusts resulted across portions of northeast and north central South Dakota.
episodes.180251: Storms pushed through NW MN and some in NE ND, but the strongest storms were in Minnesota. Wind gusts around 60 MPH and hail were reported.
episodes.180259: Storms produce gusty outflow winds across the area.
episodes.180321: A weak low pressure system served as the focal point for small, scattered and slow-moving thunderstorms across far northeastern South Dakota during the afternoon of June 5th. A brief landspout tornado was observed north of Summit and south of Sisseton around 2:45 pm. No damage was reported.
episodes.180330: Snowmelt resultant flooding from April continued through May and into June along the very slowly draining James River in South Dakota. While flood levels continued to decrease from their crest in April, minor flooding persisted into June in some locations, slowly falling through the month. This flooding mainly impacted agricultural land.
episodes.180506: Enhanced by an upper-level trough, scattered showers and thunderstorms over the coastal waters near the Upper Florida Keys resulted in isolated gale-force wind gusts.
episodes.180683: A continued active pattern resulted in additional scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms to finish out the month of May, with some resulting in damage due to strong gusts.
episodes.180802: Two different rounds of showers and thunderstorms overtook the combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles on the afternoon and evening of May 31st. The wave of storms produced severe wind gusts between 58 and 60 mph through the northwest TX Panhandle  and portions of the Oklahoma Panhandle. The second wave of storms moved into the southwest TX Panhandle from eastern New Mexico later in the evening. These storms produced severe winds between 58 and 63 mph, as well as hail up to the size of nickels. They also were heavy rain producers which led to some urban flooding in the east side of Canyon, TX as well as portions of Amarillo, TX.
episodes.180910: Afternoon thunderstorms formed south of Douglas and eventually merged into a small line which produced severe hail and wind gusts.
episodes.180958: A band of thunderstorms developed during the afternoon along a trailing boundary which extended from a subtle upper-level impulse that lifted from South Dakota into North Dakota.  A couple stronger cells in the line produced some penny- to nickel-sized hail.
episodes.181179: Scattered thunderstorms occurred across the coastal waters, a few of which produced gusty winds in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.181246: Heavy rain fell on May 31st leading to flash flooding in Miami and Leavenworth Counties.
episodes.181314: Despite the presence of broad upper ridging, an extension of the subtropical jet stream across the Southern Plains fostered widespread (mostly sub-severe) convection across the forecast area. A few damaging wind reports were received associated with the strongest storms.
episodes.181335: The combination of westerly flow aloft, moderate to strong instability and a dryline resulted in scattered severe thunderstorms across portions of west central Texas. A few the storms were supercell thunderstorms, which merged into a line of thunderstorms while moving east across the area. The severe storms produced large hail and isolated damaging winds.
episodes.181512: June began with river flooding along Clear Creek near Chinook, which reached Major Flood Stage for the second time this spring. In fact, Clear Creek recorded its third highest crest on record, as of writing. Fergus County, especially locations south of Lewistown, also experienced flooding due to heavy rainfall. Elsewhere, isolated severe thunderstorms occurred as a spring-like storm system moved across the area.
episodes.181578: A few short-lived storms developed in east central Minnesota, and there were two reports of sub-severe hail.
episodes.181742: A severe thunderstorm produced hail up to quarter size in Elbert County.
episodes.181890: Heavy rain led to a very localized flash flood in rural Johnson County.
episodes.182684: In the middle afternoon of the the first, a cluster of storms developed in eastern Colorado and produced penny sized hail in Burlington.
episodes.182716: Large hail and flash flooding occurred in the southern mountains.
episodes.182795: Extreme snowmelt from heavy snowfall and extreme flows on the Portneuf River caused damage to the Chesterfield Reservoir spillway.  The old structure started to deconstruct and makeshift repairs were made to alleviate any significant flooding.   Cost to repair the damaged structure were estimated at around 1.5 million dollars.
episodes.182802: Flooding due to the rise of the Big Wood River due to snowmelt and spring rains flooded parts of Hailey including War Eagle Drive, Flat Top Road, and Camp Creek Road.   Damages were estimated at 1.9 million dollars on Flat Top Road and Camp Creek Road.
episodes.182835: A tropical disturbance over the region coupled with an upper level low pressure over the Gulf of Mexico led to several strong thunderstorms over the South Florida Atlantic waters.
episodes.182838: A tropical disturbance over the region coupled with an upper level low pressure over the Gulf of Mexico led to several strong thunderstorms over the South Florida Atlantic waters.
episodes.183025: Storms pushed through NW MN and some in NE ND. Wind gusts around 60 MPH and hail were reported.
episodes.188964: A weather front brought from 1 to 2 inches of rain to the headwaters of Birch Creek and Crooked Creek. The rain fell on a residual winter snowpack and resulted in significant runoff due to the combination of rapid snowmelt and the heavy rainfall. This caused high water and flooding along rivers and streams draining the region including Crooked Creek and Birch Creek which impacted the community of Central and portions of the Steese Highway. Flooding continued into early June.
episodes.188969: A weather front brought from 1 to 2 inches of rain to the headwaters of Birch Creek and Crooked Creek. The rain fell on a residual winter snowpack and resulted in significant runoff due to the combination of rapid snowmelt and the heavy rainfall. This caused high water and flooding along rivers and streams draining the region including Crooked Creek and Birch Creek which impacted the community of Central and portions of the Steese Highway. Flooding started in late May and continued into early June.

Numerous reports came in for water covering roads, with fast flowing water leading to numerous roads being impassable in several areas. Drainage  ditches and playa lakes began overflowing onto  roads and encroaching on homes in the  southwest side of Amarillo.

The James River near Columbia, CMBS2, started the month in moderate flood stage at 17.31 feet, then steadily dropped through the month. It reached minor flood stage of <16 feet from June 20th through early on June 24th before rising back into moderate flood stage thereafter due to heavy rains, and remained in moderate flood stage through the rest of the month. Significant amounts of agricultural lands remained flooded through the month.

The James River near Stratford, SFDS2, started the month in moderate flood stage at 17.32 feet, then steadily dropped through the month. It reached minor flood stage of <17 feet on June 11th, and remained in there through the rest of the month. Significant amounts of agricultural lands remained flooded through the month, and county roads were flooded.

The James River near Ashton, ATNS2, started the month in moderate flood stage at 15.42 feet, then steadily dropped through the month. It reached minor flood stage of <14 feet on June 12th, and then remained there through the rest of the month. Significant amounts of farm land were flooded, including crop and pasture land.

Heavy rain and snowmelt in the Birch Creek headwaters caused Birch Creek to flow overbank and flood portions of the Steese Highway between milepost 145 to 147. The flooding caused the highway to be closed for a period of time due to dangerous driving conditions. Birch Creek fell back within bank on June 2nd.

Thunderstorms with heavy rainfall became anchored over Lynn County during the mid-morning hours. The Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near O'Donnell measured 7.02 inches of rainfall. The intense rain rates and amount of rainfall resulted in the closure of a portion of US Highway 87 between O'Donnell and Tahoka. Numerous water rescues were completed and many vehicles became stranded in the flood waters.

Thunderstorms that became anchored over Lynn County bringing extensive flash flooding slowly moved into central and northern Garza County spreading intense rain rates along with it. Widespread flash flooding was reported throughout central and northern Garza County. Additionally, a tractor trailer rolled over on US Highway 84 near Farm to Market Road 399 also causing a multiple vehicle wreck.
